intent: To demonstrate that bail is unaffordable for the majority of defendants at their initial hearing.

units.meaning: Only 14% of people given bail were able to pay at their initial hearing.

basis.note: Table value is 14 in percent units; relative_value is 0.14.

accepted_routes: Only 14% of people given bail could pay at the initial hearing.
14% were able to pay bail at the initial hearing.
units.visual_evidence_rule: A chart label or annotation must show 14% for the able-to-pay bail category.
units.temporal_anchor: The narration clause 'only 14% of people given bail were able to pay at their initial hearing'.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video explicitly state the 14% able-to-pay share, or is the 86% unable share alone sufficient?

units.meaning: 86% of people given bail were unable to pay at their initial hearing, making nonpayment the majority outcome.

basis.note: Table value is 86 in percent units; relative_value is 0.86.

accepted_routes: 86% of people given bail were unable to pay at the initial hearing.
A majority—86%—could not pay bail at the initial hearing.
units.visual_evidence_rule: A chart label or annotation must show 86% for the unable-to-pay bail category.
units.temporal_anchor: The final 'initial hearing' clause, following or paired with the 14% able-to-pay statement.
units.reviewer_question: Is the 86% unable-to-pay majority required to be explicitly shown, or can it be left as the complement of 14%?

units.meaning: The unable-to-pay share is 72 percentage points higher than the able-to-pay share (86% vs 14%).
accepted_routes: The unable-to-pay share exceeds the able-to-pay share by 72 percentage points.
The gap is 72 points: 86% unable versus 14% able.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Either both 86% and 14% labels must be visible, or a difference annotation must show 72 percentage points.
units.temporal_anchor: After the narration's 14% clause, when contrasting inability with ability.
units.reviewer_question: Should the 72-percentage-point gap be required, or is showing the two shares side by side enough?

units.meaning: The unable-to-pay group is about 6.1 times as common as the able-to-pay group (86% / 14%).
accepted_routes: Unable-to-pay is about 6.1 times as common as able-to-pay.
There were roughly 6 times as many unable-to-pay cases as able-to-pay cases.
The 86% unable group is more than six times the 14% able group.
units.visual_evidence_rule: A ratio annotation or both percentage labels must be visible so the 86:14 comparison can be read.
units.temporal_anchor: Optional emphasis after the 14% and 86% shares are established.
units.reviewer_question: Is the about-6x ratio worth requiring as a derived comparison, or is it optional enrichment?

units.meaning: The able-to-pay and unable-to-pay shares sum to 100% of people given bail (14% + 86%).
accepted_routes: Together, 14% able and 86% unable account for 100% of people given bail.
The two bail outcomes sum to the full 100%: 14% plus 86%.
The composition is complete: 14% able, 86% unable.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must show both shares as parts of a whole, such as a donut or 100% stacked bar.
units.temporal_anchor: When the donut composition is displayed, after both share labels appear.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video make the 100% whole or complete partition explicit, or is that only a chart-design convention?

optional_valid: Describe the chart as a donut composition of people given bail at the initial hearing.
State that the denominator is people given bail, not all defendants or all Americans.
Use the complement relationship: 86% unable is the remainder after 14% able.
unsupported_to_avoid: the narration's dollar bail amount (not in table)
the narration's analysis year (not in table)
New York City Jails setting (not in table)
national or demographic extrapolation beyond the table
causal claims that bail causes poverty or missed hearings
notes: Core required content is the 14% able and 86% unable shares; derived gap, ratio, and 100% sum are optional but valid. Avoid the narration's untabled numeric and geographic details.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
